# Stop AI coding agents installing hallucinated packages

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-agent-hallucinated-packages/


**ExactGround is a free, open-source guard for AI coding agents.** It runs as a hook in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor. Before an `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `npx`, `pip`, `uv`, `poetry` or `pdm` install command it can parse runs, it checks each package name against the public npm registry and PyPI. Names that do not exist, versions that were never published, and young look-alikes of popular packages are blocked. Source and install: [github.com/alidaram99/exactground](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground).

## Why agents need this

A USENIX Security 2025 study generated 2.23 million code samples with 16 models. **19.7% referenced at least one package that does not exist**, and 43% of the invented names came back on every rerun of the same prompt ([paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/spracklen)). Because the names are predictable, attackers can register them with malware. This is called *slopsquatting*.

A rule in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` saying "never invent packages" is text the model may ignore. A hook is code that runs on every install.

## Try it in one line

```console
$ npx -y github:alidaram99/exactground#v0.1.2 check pypi:requests pypi:reqeusts react@99.0.0
OK      pypi:requests
BLOCK   pypi:reqeusts — "reqeusts" does not exist on PyPI; did you mean "requests"? (it is 1 edit away)
BLOCK   react@99.0.0 — version 99.0.0 of "react" was never published (latest is 19.3.0)
```

## Install it in your agent

- **Claude Code:** `claude plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground`, then `claude plugin install exactground@exactground-marketplace`.
- **Codex:** `codex plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground --ref v0.1.2`, then trust the hook in `/hooks`.
- **Gemini CLI and Cursor:** `exactground init gemini --write` or `exactground init cursor --write` in your project.

Installs hidden inside `node -e`, `python -c`, `$(...)` or `eval` cannot be checked, so the hook denies them. If the registry or the checker fails, it denies too.

Bare installs such as `npm install`, `uv sync` and `poetry install` are checked against the lockfile, so a dependency the agent wrote into `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` is caught too.

## Check that an API exists in your exact version

Many hallucinations are real packages used wrongly. `useActionState` does not exist in React 18, and `numpy.asfarray` was removed in NumPy 2.0. The hosted ExactGround API answers these questions from the published package itself:
- npm: `.d.ts` declarations, read with the TypeScript compiler.
- Python: wheels, parsed statically and never executed.

Status: awaiting publication on the Apify Store; until the Store page loads, the MCP URL answers only its owner.

It is an MCP server billed per check:
- `check_symbols`: $0.002 per symbol.
- `check_packages`: $0.0005 per package.
- `check_diff`: $0.01 per diff.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http exactground https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN"
```

**[Open ExactGround on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api)** · [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)

# App Store Reviews Scraper: any app, no Connect key

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/


The **App Store Connect API** only gives you reviews for apps your team owns, and it needs a private key. To read what users say about **any** app, including competitors, in any storefront, this Actor collects reviews from Apple's public customer-review feed and adds the app's public metadata. It needs no login and no Connect key.

## What you get

**One row per review:**

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| `appId`, `appName`, `country` | `570060128`, `Duolingo: Language Lessons`, `us` |
| `reviewId`, `title`, `text`, `rating` (1–5) | `14612250135`, `Fun`, `Very fun and…`, `5` |
| `version`, `date`, `userName` | `7.142.0`, `2026-09-30T13:01:34-07:00`, `…` |
| `voteCount`, `voteSum` | helpfulness votes |

**Optionally, one app-details row per app × country:** name, developer, price and currency, average rating, rating count, version, release dates, genres, content rating, size, minimum OS and description.

App-details row from a real run:

```json
{
  "type": "app",
  "appId": "570060128",
  "country": "us",
  "name": "Duolingo: Language Lessons",
  "developer": "Duolingo, Inc",
  "price": 0,
  "currency": "USD",
  "averageRating": 4.72302,
  "ratingCount": 5481026,
  "version": "7.142.0",
  "currentVersionReleaseDate": "2026-09-28T17:42:01Z",
  "genres": ["Education", "Social Networking"],
  "contentRating": "4+",
  "url": "https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duolingo-language-lessons/id570060128?uo=4"
}
```

## Use cases

- **ASO and product feedback:** pull every recent review of your app into a spreadsheet or database and track ratings by version.
- **Competitor monitoring:** watch a competitor's rating, review volume and release cadence across countries.
- **Market research:** compare what users complain about across the top apps in a category and storefront.

## Run it in the Apify Console (no code)

1. Open the **[App Store Reviews Scraper](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)** and click **Try for free**.
2. Paste App Store URLs or numeric app ids, for example `https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duolingo-language-lessons/id570060128` or `570060128`.
3. Choose countries (`us`, `gb`, `de`…), the maximum number of reviews per app, and optionally a `sinceDate`.
4. Click **Start**, then export the dataset as CSV, Excel or JSON.

## Run it from code

Replace `<owner>/app-store-reviews` with the Actor id shown on its Store page.

### Node.js (`apify-client`)

```js
import { ApifyClient } from 'apify-client';

const client = new ApifyClient({ token: process.env.APIFY_TOKEN });

const run = await client.actor('<owner>/app-store-reviews').call({
  apps: ['570060128'], countries: ['us'], maxReviewsPerApp: 50, includeAppDetails: true,
});
const { items } = await client.dataset(run.defaultDatasetId).listItems();
for (const row of items) console.log(row.type, row.type === 'app' ? `${row.name} ★${row.averageRating}` : `${row.rating}★ ${row.title}`);
```

### Python (`apify-client` ≥ 3)

```python
import os
from apify_client import ApifyClient

client = ApifyClient(os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])
run = client.actor("<owner>/app-store-reviews").call(
    run_input={"apps": ["570060128"], "countries": ["us", "gb"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200},
)
for item in client.dataset(run.default_dataset_id).list_items().items:
    print(item["type"], item.get("rating"), item.get("title"))
```

### curl (one call, results in the response)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/<owner>~app-store-reviews/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"apps":["570060128"],"countries":["us"],"maxReviewsPerApp":50}'
```

## Limits

- **Up to 500 reviews per app per country.** Apple's public feed stops there (10 pages × 50). To get more coverage, add more `countries`, since reviews differ by storefront.
- Developer replies are not part of Apple's public feed, so `developerResponse` is always `null`.
- Reviews come newest first. `sinceDate` stops paging once older reviews are reached.

## Pricing

**$0.20 per 1,000 rows** ($0.0002 per review or app-details row), pay per event. You pay only for rows delivered, with no subscription.

**[Open the App Store Reviews Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)**

# Azure Content Moderator Alternative: ProcessText/Screen

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/


Microsoft's [Content Moderator overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/overview) says the service has been deprecated since February 2024 and **retires on March 15, 2027**. The product [lifecycle page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/azure-ai-content-moderator) lists April 1, 2027. The suggested successor, **Azure AI Content Safety**, is a different API with a different URL, request and response (severity levels for Hate/Sexual/SelfHarm/Violence). Code that reads `Terms`, `PII` and `Classification.Category1/2/3` has to be rewritten.

This page shows a **wire-compatible replacement for the text screen endpoint**, so that code keeps working. You call the same `POST /contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen` with the same query string and raw-text body, and get back the same response JSON.

## What changes in your code

1. The endpoint: `https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com` becomes `https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor`.
2. Authentication: send your [Apify API token](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) as `Authorization: Bearer …` or `?token=…`. An `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` header is accepted and ignored.

### curl

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True&token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255.255.255.255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052'
```

That is Microsoft's own documentation example. Our response matches Microsoft's published `NormalizedText`, the `Terms` entry (`crap` at Index 10) and every PII index:

```json
{
  "OriginalText": "Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255.255.255.255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052",
  "NormalizedText": "Is this a crap email abcdef@ abcd. com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255. 255. 255. 255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052",
  "Misrepresentation": null,
  "PII": {
    "Email": [{ "Detected": "abcdef@abcd.com", "SubType": "Regular", "Text": "abcdef@abcd.com", "Index": 21 }],
    "SSN": [],
    "IPA": [{ "SubType": "IPV4", "Text": "255.255.255.255", "Index": 61 }],
    "Phone": [{ "CountryCode": "US", "Text": "6657789887", "Index": 45 }],
    "Address": [{ "Text": "1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052", "Index": 78 }]
  },
  "Classification": {
    "ReviewRecommended": true,
    "Category1": { "Score": 0.0023 },
    "Category2": { "Score": 0.2708 },
    "Category3": { "Score": 0.9562 }
  },
  "Language": "eng",
  "Terms": [{ "Index": 10, "OriginalIndex": 10, "ListId": 0, "Term": "crap" }],
  "Status": { "Code": 3000, "Description": "OK", "Exception": null },
  "TrackingId": "…"
}
```

### C# (`HttpClient`, .NET 6+)

```csharp
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;

var baseUrl = "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor";
var token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("APIFY_TOKEN")!;

using var http = new HttpClient();
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);

var content = new StringContent("Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?", Encoding.UTF8, "text/plain");
var response = await http.PostAsync(
    $"{baseUrl}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True", content);
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
var root = json.RootElement;
Console.WriteLine($"Status {root.GetProperty("Status").GetProperty("Code").GetInt32()}, " +
                  $"Category3 {root.GetProperty("Classification").GetProperty("Category3").GetProperty("Score").GetDouble():F3}, " +
                  $"first term '{root.GetProperty("Terms")[0].GetProperty("Term").GetString()}'");
// Status 3000, Category3 0.971, first term 'crap'
```

If you use the old `Microsoft.Azure.CognitiveServices.ContentModerator` SDK, set `client.Endpoint` to the Standby URL and pass `ServiceClientCredentials` that add the `Authorization: Bearer` header. *We tested the REST path above, not that SDK.*

### Python (`requests`)

```python
import os
import requests

BASE = "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor"
APIFY_TOKEN = os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"]

r = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen",
    params={"language": "eng", "classify": "True", "PII": "True"},
    headers={"Content-Type": "text/plain", "Authorization": f"Bearer {APIFY_TOKEN}"},
    data="This is crap, email me at someone@example.com".encode("utf-8"),
)
screen = r.json()
print(screen["Status"]["Code"], screen["Classification"]["Category3"]["Score"],
      [t["Term"] for t in screen["Terms"] or []], [e["Text"] for e in screen["PII"]["Email"]])
# 3000 0.98 ['crap'] ['someone@example.com']
```

### Node.js (`fetch`)

```js
const BASE = 'https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor';
const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain', Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}` },
  body: 'You are a worthless idiot',
});
const screen = await res.json();
console.log(screen.Status.Code, screen.Classification.ReviewRecommended, screen.Classification.Category3.Score);
// 3000 true 0.997
```

## What is identical, approximate, or unsupported

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Route, method, query parameters (case-insensitive), `text/plain`/`html`/`xml`/`markdown` bodies, 1,024-character limit | **Identical** |
| Field names, casing and order; `Status` 3000; `Terms: null` when clean; `Misrepresentation: null`; `TrackingId` | **Identical** |
| `NormalizedText`; `Terms` `Index` and `OriginalIndex` offsets | Identical on Microsoft's documented examples. Unusual inputs may normalize differently |
| `PII` (Email, IPA, Phone, Address, SSN) | Same shape. Patterns are deliberately strict: US/UK phones, US addresses with state and ZIP |
| Built-in profanity list (`ListId 0`) | Same format. The word list is open (LDNOOBW, CC-BY-4.0, 24 languages), so matches can differ from Azure's private list |
| `Classification` Category1 (explicit), Category3 (offensive) | **Approximate.** Open Detoxify model; scores differ from Azure's |
| `Classification` Category2 (suggestive) | **Approximate proxy:** `max(Category1, 0.3 × obscene)`. Flirty but clean text is not detected |
| `ReviewRecommended` | True when any category is ≥ 0.5. Azure's own thresholds were never published |
| Classification for non-English text | Omitted, as in Azure |
| `autocorrect=true` | Accepted. The field is returned, but no spelling correction is applied |
| Custom term lists (`listId`), image/video moderation, list management, review tool | **Not supported** |

## Pricing

**$1 per 1,000 screened texts**, pay per event. Requests that fail validation are not charged. There is no subscription, and you can cap spending per run on Apify (`429 TooManyRequests` at the cap).

## FAQ

**Should I just move to Content Safety?** If you can rewrite the integration and re-tune thresholds, yes, that is a fine path. This replacement is for teams whose code, stored results and dashboards depend on the old response format.

**Do you store text?** No. Nothing is written to disk or logged.

**Short non-English texts?** Latin-script text under 40 characters is treated as English. Pass `language=spa`, `language=deu` and so on to use the right profanity list.

## Get started

**[Azure Content Moderator drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat)**: copy its Standby URL and your token, then change the endpoint in your code.

# Drop-in replacements for retiring APIs, plus data tools

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/


Three widely used APIs are being switched off between December 2026 and March 2027. Their official successors use **different requests and responses**, so every integration has to be rewritten. The tools below accept **the same request and return the same response shape** as the API you already call. You change the host, add an Apify token, and keep your code.

They run on [Apify](https://apify.com) and are billed per use, with no subscription. Each one says clearly what is identical, what is approximate and what is not supported.

## Drop-in replacements

### Google Perspective API (ends after 31 Dec 2026)
`POST /v1alpha1/comments:analyze`, with TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, PROFANITY, IDENTITY_ATTACK, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT and SEVERE_TOXICITY, in 7 languages. Google's own Python client works with only the discovery URL changed. Scores come from open models: close to Perspective's, not identical.
**$1 per 1,000 comments** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/perspective-compat)

### Azure Content Moderator, text screen (retires 15 Mar 2027)
`POST /contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen`, with the same `Terms`, `PII`, `Classification` and `Status` JSON. It matches Microsoft's own documented example field for field. Category scores are approximate, and custom term lists are not supported.
**$1 per 1,000 texts** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat)

### OpenAI whisper-1 (removed 26 Feb 2027)
`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/translations`, with SRT, VTT, and word and segment timestamps. It works with the official OpenAI Python and Node SDKs by changing `base_url` and `api_key`. It uses the smaller open Whisper model (about 4% word error on clear English), with up to 10 minutes per file.
**$0.006 per minute** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/whisper-compat)

## Data tools

### App Store reviews
Reviews and app details for any app in any country, from Apple's public feed, with no App Store Connect key. Up to 500 reviews per app per country.
**$0.20 per 1,000 rows** · [Guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)

### Woolworths Australia prices
Shelf price, specials and unit price per kg or litre, by search term, from public catalog data.
**$1 per 1,000 products** · [Guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/woolworths-api/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/woolworths-au-products)

## How it works

1. Create a free Apify account and copy your API token.
2. Open the tool on the Apify Store. For the API replacements, copy its **Standby URL**.
3. Point your existing code at that URL and send the token. Pay only for what you use, and set a spending cap if you like.

Nothing you send is stored: comments, texts and audio are processed in memory and discarded.

# Perspective API Alternative: drop-in comments:analyze

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/


Google Jigsaw's **Perspective API** (`commentanalyzer.googleapis.com`) is being sunset. The [official site](https://perspectiveapi.com/) says the service ends after **December 31, 2026**, with no migration path. Every forum, comment section, Discord bot and research pipeline that calls `comments:analyze` will start getting errors.

This page shows how to keep that code working with a **wire-compatible replacement**. You send the same `POST /v1alpha1/comments:analyze` body and get back the same JSON: `attributeScores.TOXICITY.summaryScore.value`, `spanScores`, `languages`, `clientToken`, and Google-style error envelopes. **The scores come from open-source models, so they are close to Perspective's but not identical**. See [How the scores compare](#how-the-scores-compare) before you switch production thresholds.

## What breaks on January 1, 2027

- Any request to `https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze` (REST, `googleapiclient`, the `perspective-api-client` npm package, the R `peRspective` package, and so on).
- Plugins that hard-code that host, such as the Discourse plugin and many Discord moderation bots.
- Benchmarks and research code that use Perspective's TOXICITY score as a metric.

## The migration

Your new endpoint is the Actor's Standby URL, `https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor`. You authenticate with your [Apify API token](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations), either as `?token=…` or as `Authorization: Bearer …`. The Google `key=` parameter is accepted and ignored.

### curl / any HTTP client

```bash
# Before: https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze?key=$GOOGLE_KEY
curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor/v1alpha1/comments:analyze?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"comment":{"text":"You are an idiot"},"requestedAttributes":{"TOXICITY":{},"INSULT":{}},"languages":["en"]}'
```

Response (real output from our test run):

```json
{
  "attributeScores": {
    "TOXICITY": {
      "spanScores": [{ "begin": 0, "end": 16, "score": { "value": 0.99683121, "type": "PROBABILITY" } }],
      "summaryScore": { "value": 0.99683121, "type": "PROBABILITY" }
    },
    "INSULT": {
      "spanScores": [{ "begin": 0, "end": 16, "score": { "value": 0.9958577, "type": "PROBABILITY" } }],
      "summaryScore": { "value": 0.9958577, "type": "PROBABILITY" }
    }
  },
  "languages": ["en"],
  "detectedLanguages": ["en"]
}
```

### Python: Google's own `google-api-python-client`

Keep your Perspective quickstart code. Only the `build()` call changes: point `discoveryServiceUrl` at the Actor and pass your Apify token as credentials.

```python
import os
from googleapiclient import discovery
from google.oauth2.credentials import Credentials

BASE = "https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor"
APIFY_TOKEN = os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"]

client = discovery.build(
    "commentanalyzer", "v1alpha1",
    credentials=Credentials(APIFY_TOKEN),  # was: developerKey=GOOGLE_API_KEY
    discoveryServiceUrl=BASE + "/$discovery/rest?version={apiVersion}&token=" + APIFY_TOKEN,
    static_discovery=False,
)
response = client.comments().analyze(body={
    "comment": {"text": "friendly greetings from python"},
    "requestedAttributes": {"TOXICITY": {}},
}).execute()
print(response["attributeScores"]["TOXICITY"]["summaryScore"]["value"])  # 0.01015937
```

### Node.js: plain `fetch`

```js
const BASE = 'https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor';
const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/v1alpha1/comments:analyze`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ comment: { text: 'You are an idiot' }, requestedAttributes: { TOXICITY: {} } }),
});
const data = await res.json();
console.log(data.attributeScores.TOXICITY.summaryScore.value); // 0.99683121
```

### Node.js: the `perspective-api-client` npm package

The package hard-codes Google's URL and **bundles its own copy of axios**, so an interceptor on your app's `axios` has no effect. Attach the redirect to the axios instance the library actually loads, once at startup:

```js
const libAxios = require(require.resolve('axios', { paths: [require.resolve('perspective-api-client')] }));
const BASE = 'https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor';

libAxios.interceptors.request.use((cfg) => {
  if (cfg.url && cfg.url.startsWith('https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com')) {
    cfg.url = cfg.url.replace('https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com', BASE);
    cfg.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}`;
  }
  return cfg;
});

// unchanged application code:
const Perspective = require('perspective-api-client');
const perspective = new Perspective({ apiKey: 'unused-but-required-by-the-library' });
perspective.analyze('You are a complete moron', { attributes: ['toxicity', 'insult'] })
  .then((r) => console.log(r.attributeScores.TOXICITY.summaryScore.value)); // 0.99700852
```

### Discourse (`discourse-perspective-api`)

The plugin keeps the API key as a site setting, but the host is the constant `GOOGLE_API_DOMAIN = "https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com"` in `lib/discourse_perspective.rb`. In a fork, change that constant to your Standby URL and append `token=<APIFY_TOKEN>` to the request query. The plugin's models (`TOXICITY`, `SEVERE_TOXICITY`) and thresholds work as before. *We have not run this inside a live Discourse instance. The request and response format is what we tested.*

Other wrappers that already accept a base URL (for example GateNLP's Perspective client) only need the URL and the token.

## Supported attributes and languages

| Attribute | en | es fr it pt ru tr | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| TOXICITY, SEVERE_TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, IDENTITY_ATTACK | ✅ | ✅ | |
| PROFANITY | ✅ | ✅ | Approximated from the model's "obscene" output |
| SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT | ✅ | — | English only, as in Perspective |
| `*_EXPERIMENTAL` aliases | ✅ | ✅ | Served by the matching base attribute and returned under the name you requested |
| FLIRTATION, the NYT models, bridging attributes | ❌ | ❌ | Returns Perspective's own `LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_ATTRIBUTE` error |

The language is detected automatically when you leave out `languages`. Other languages get Perspective's standard "does not support request languages" error, so your existing fallback code keeps working. `spanAnnotations`, `scoreThreshold`, `clientToken` and snake_case field names are supported. The limit is 20 KB of text per comment.

## How the scores compare

The scores come from [Detoxify](https://github.com/unitaryai/detoxify), open models trained on the same Jigsaw/Civil Comments data family that Perspective came from. They run as quantized ONNX on CPU inside the Actor: `unbiased-toxic-roberta` for English and `multilingual-toxic-xlm-roberta` for the other six languages.

- Clear cases agree. In our tests, abusive text scored 0.99+ and polite text scored under 0.02.
- **Borderline comments can differ** from Perspective by a noticeable margin. We have not run a side-by-side calibration against the live Perspective API.
- If you auto-hide comments at a high threshold (0.85–0.9), you will probably see similar behavior. If you act at low thresholds, run a sample of your own comments through the Actor's batch mode first and re-tune.

## Pricing

**$1 per 1,000 analyzed comments**, pay per event. Failed requests (4xx) are not charged. There is no subscription, and you can cap spending per run on Apify. When you reach your limit, the API answers `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`.

## FAQ

**Is this Google?** No. It is an independent service that implements the public `commentanalyzer` v1alpha1 interface.

**Do you store comments?** No. Text is scored in memory and discarded.

**Latency?** The model takes about 10–30 ms per comment on a warm instance. After about 5 minutes without traffic the instance sleeps, and the next request waits a few seconds while it starts.

**Why do I need an Apify token?** Apify hosts the service and bills per call. The token identifies your account. It is the only new thing your code needs.

## Get started

Open the Actor on the Apify Store, then copy its Standby URL and your token: **[Perspective API drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/perspective-compat)**.

# whisper-1 alternative with SRT, VTT and word timestamps

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/


OpenAI's [deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) schedules **`whisper-1` for removal on February 26, 2027**. Its successors are not drop-in. Apps built on whisper-1 features have to change: subtitles through `response_format=srt` or `vtt`, `timestamp_granularities[]=word` and `segment`, and `/v1/audio/translations`.

This page shows how to keep exactly that API: `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations`, the same multipart fields, and the same `json`, `text`, `srt`, `vtt` and `verbose_json` responses. It works with the **official OpenAI SDKs**. You change `base_url` and `api_key`, and nothing else.

## Python: official `openai` SDK

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://dropin-apis--whisper-compat.apify.actor/v1",   # was: default api.openai.com
    api_key=os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"],           # your Apify token, sent as Authorization: Bearer
)

with open("armstrong.ogg", "rb") as f:
    srt = client.audio.transcriptions.create(model="whisper-1", file=f, response_format="srt")
print(srt)

with open("armstrong.ogg", "rb") as f:
    verbose = client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="whisper-1", file=f, response_format="verbose_json",
        timestamp_granularities=["word", "segment"],
    )
for w in verbose.words[:5]:
    print(f"{w.start:6.2f}-{w.end:6.2f}  {w.word}")
print(len(verbose.segments), "segments,", verbose.duration, "seconds")
```

Real output on NASA's public-domain Apollo 11 clip ("one small step"):

```text
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:05,000
I'm going to step off the limb now.

2
00:00:15,000 --> 00:00:18,000
That's one small step for man.

3
00:00:20,000 --> 00:00:24,000
One giant leap for mankind.

  3.22-  3.96  I'm
  3.96-  4.06  going
  4.06-  4.18  to
  4.18-  4.34  step
  4.34-  4.58  off
3 segments, 24.11 seconds
```

(Armstrong said "the LEM". The small model heard "limb", which is the kind of error to expect, see Limits below.)

> Pass the token only as `api_key`. If you append `?token=…` to `base_url`, the SDK adds the route after the query string and the request goes to the wrong URL.

## Node.js: official `openai` SDK

```js
import fs from 'node:fs';
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: 'https://dropin-apis--whisper-compat.apify.actor/v1',
  apiKey: process.env.APIFY_TOKEN,
});

const vtt = await client.audio.transcriptions.create({
  model: 'whisper-1',
  file: fs.createReadStream('armstrong.ogg'),
  response_format: 'vtt',
});
console.log(vtt); // WEBVTT ... 00:00:15.000 --> 00:00:18.000  That's one small step for man.
```

## curl: word timestamps

```bash
curl -s "https://dropin-apis--whisper-compat.apify.actor/v1/audio/transcriptions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -F model=whisper-1 \
  -F response_format=verbose_json \
  -F 'timestamp_granularities[]=word' \
  -F file=@armstrong.ogg
```

The response is OpenAI's `verbose_json` shape: `task`, `language` (`"english"`), `duration`, `text`, `words[]` (`word`, `start`, `end`) and `usage` (`{"type":"duration","seconds":25}`). `segments[]` is included when you request `segment` granularity, which is the default.

## Compatibility

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, `GET /v1/models` | ✅ |
| Fields `file`, `model` (`whisper-1`), `language`, `prompt`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `timestamp_granularities[]` | ✅ Same names, defaults and validation |
| `json` (+ `usage`), `text`, `srt`, `vtt`, `verbose_json` with segments and words | ✅ |
| OpenAI error envelope (`{"error":{"message","type","param","code"}}`) | ✅ |
| `stream`, `include`, `chunking_strategy`, `diarized_json`, gpt-4o / gpt-transcribe models | ❌ (whisper-1 didn't support them either) |

## Limits: read before switching

- **Model:** Whisper **small** (multilingual) running with faster-whisper/CTranslate2 int8 on CPU, beam size 5. OpenAI's whisper-1 is the much larger Whisper V2. On clean English (LibriSpeech) we measured **about 4% word error rate**. Expect more errors on noisy audio, heavy accents and less common languages.
- **Length:** up to **10 minutes and 25 MB per request**. Longer files get `400 audio_too_long`, so split them first, for example `ffmpeg -i in.mp3 -f segment -segment_time 540 out%03d.mp3`.
- **Speed:** about 4 seconds of audio per second of compute. A 1-minute file takes about 12 s and a 10-minute file about 2.5 min. Each instance handles one file at a time. A busy instance answers `429 rate_limit_exceeded`, which the OpenAI SDKs retry automatically.
- **Cold start:** after about 5 minutes without traffic the instance sleeps, and the next request waits a few seconds extra.

## Pricing

**$0.006 per minute, billed per started 15 seconds** ($0.0015 per 15 s). OpenAI billed whisper-1 at $0.006 per minute rounded to the second, so the two prices match on whole 15-second blocks. A clip under 15 seconds costs $0.0015 here instead of about $0.001. Failed requests are not charged. If you set a spending cap, a file the remaining budget can't cover is refused *before* it is transcribed (`429 insufficient_quota`).

## FAQ

**Is this OpenAI?** No. It is an independent service that runs OpenAI's open-source Whisper model (MIT license) behind the same API shape.

**Do you keep my audio?** No. Audio is decoded in memory, transcribed and discarded.

**Languages?** All 99 Whisper languages, with auto-detection. Passing `language` (ISO-639-1) improves speed and accuracy.

## Get started

**[whisper-1 drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/whisper-compat)**: copy the Standby URL into `base_url` and use your Apify token as `api_key`.

# Woolworths API: Australian grocery prices as JSON

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/woolworths-api/


Woolworths has no public product API. This Actor collects **public catalog data** from Woolworths Australia's own product search: shelf price, was-price and specials, and the **unit price** (per kg, per litre, per 100 g). You give it search terms and get one clean row per product.

## What you get

Row from a real run (search term `milk`):

```json
{
  "stockcode": "888137",
  "name": "Woolworths Full Cream Milk",
  "brand": "Woolworths",
  "description": "Woolworths Full Cream Milk 2L",
  "packageSize": "2L",
  "price": 3.4,
  "wasPrice": 3.4,
  "isOnSpecial": false,
  "savingsAmount": 0,
  "cupPrice": 1.7,
  "cupMeasure": "1L",
  "cupString": "$1.70 / 1L",
  "isAvailable": true,
  "isInStock": true,
  "unit": "Each",
  "imageUrl": "https://cdn1.woolworths.media/content/wowproductimages/medium/888137.jpg",
  "productUrl": "https://www.woolworths.com.au/shop/productdetails/888137/woolworths-full-cream-milk",
  "searchTerm": "milk",
  "scrapedAt": "2026-10-02T06:14:38.625Z"
}
```

No customer data of any kind is collected.

## Use cases

- **Price monitoring:** track shelf prices and specials for your own or competing products on a schedule.
- **Inflation and basket research:** collect unit prices for staples over time.
- **Competitive pricing:** compare specials and savings across brands and ranges.

## Run it in the Apify Console (no code)

1. Open the **[Woolworths scraper](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/woolworths-au-products)** and click **Try for free**.
2. Enter search terms (`milk`, `bread`, `eggs`…), a maximum number of items per term, and a sort order.
3. Click **Start**, then download CSV, Excel or JSON. Use Apify's **Schedules** to repeat the run daily.

## Run it from code

Replace `<owner>/woolworths-au-products` with the Actor id shown on its Store page.

### Python (`apify-client` ≥ 3)

```python
import os
from apify_client import ApifyClient

client = ApifyClient(os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])

run = client.actor("<owner>/woolworths-au-products").call(
    run_input={"searchTerms": ["milk"], "maxItemsPerSearch": 3, "sortBy": "priceAsc"},
)
for item in client.dataset(run.default_dataset_id).list_items().items:
    print(item.get("name"), item.get("price"), item.get("cupString"))
# Woolworths Full Cream Milk 3.4 $1.70 / 1L
# Dairy Farmers Full Cream Milk Full Cream Milk 4.7 $2.35 / 1L
# Woolworths Full Cream Milk 4.95 $1.65 / 1L
```

### Node.js (`apify-client`)

```js
import { ApifyClient } from 'apify-client';

const client = new ApifyClient({ token: process.env.APIFY_TOKEN });
const run = await client.actor('<owner>/woolworths-au-products').call({ searchTerms: ['bread', 'eggs'], maxItemsPerSearch: 50 });
const { items } = await client.dataset(run.defaultDatasetId).listItems();
console.log(items.map((p) => `${p.name}: $${p.price} (${p.cupString})`));
```

### curl (one call, results in the response)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/<owner>~woolworths-au-products/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"searchTerms":["milk"],"maxItemsPerSearch":3,"sortBy":"priceAsc"}'
```

## Limits

- **Search terms only.** Category browsing is not implemented yet. `categoryUrls` is accepted but has no effect.
- Woolworths returns at most 36 items per page. The Actor pages through results up to `maxItemsPerSearch`.
- `sortBy` is applied by the Actor after collection, because Woolworths' own sort parameter had no effect over this interface.
- Unavailable or out-of-stock items are dropped unless you set `includeUnavailable: true`.
- If Woolworths starts blocking requests (403/429), enable Apify Proxy in the input.

## Pricing

**$1 per 1,000 products** ($0.001 per row), pay per event, with no subscription.

**[Open the Woolworths scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/woolworths-au-products)**
